The Al-Al3Ni eutectic has a eutectic temperature of 913 K and a eutectic composition of 2.9 at% Ni (6.1 wt% Ni).
The Al3Ni intermetallic phase has an orthorhombic crystal structure with common growth direction of [010].
The entropy of fusion of the Al3Ni intermetallic phase is 17.5 J/mol·K, corresponding to a Jackson factor (α) of around 2.10.
The optical microscopy experiments were performed on 10 μm thick Al-Ni films deposited on sapphire substrates.
The temperature gradient in the optical microscopy experiments was approximately 70 K/cm.
The synchrotron x-ray microscopy experiments were performed on Al-6 wt% Ni and Al-10 wt% Ni alloy samples.
The new two-zone furnace design for the synchrotron experiments allowed for temperature gradients up to 20 K/mm.
At low solidification velocities (around 0.5 μm/s), the optical microscopy revealed decoupled growth patterns with tilted, faceted Al3Ni crystals.
At intermediate velocities (around 5 μm/s), the growth transitioned to a more coupled, quasi-isothermal pattern.
At high velocities (around 10 μm/s), the faceted character of the Al3Ni crystals faded, and the growth became weakly anisotropic and rod-like.
The FIB cross-sectional analysis confirmed the transition from irregular, faceted Al3Ni crystals at low velocities to more rounded, rod-like crystals at higher velocities.

The optical microscopy observations were limited to the 2D surface-level view of the solidification front, leaving some open questions about the 3D shape and mechanisms governing the irregular-to-regular growth transition.

The Al-Al3Ni eutectic exhibits a more pronounced transition from irregular to regular growth patterns upon increasing the solidification velocity, compared to a previous study on a transparent, faceted/non-faceted eutectic system.

The in situ x-ray microscopy experiments at the synchrotron provided unprecedented nanoscale observations of the solid-liquid interface dynamics during directional solidification of the Al-Al3Ni system.

The authors correlate the morphology of the growth front patterns during solidification with the 3D shape of the Al3Ni crystals frozen in the solid, providing insights applicable to a wide array of eutectic systems containing a faceted solid phase.
